title: Implement proper multi-tenancy with per-tenant configuration
description: Tenants are configured from a JSON document (a file or inline), each with its own database and AOS connection, supporting both AOS topologies per tenant: a dedicated AOS instance, or a shared AOS instance with AOS multi-tenancy addressed via X-Tenant-ID. Payment providers, mail, Mattermost, OAuth applications, the web-push signing identity, file storage and browser-exposed variables are declared per tenant, and nothing is inherited from the environment or from another tenant; the few settings bound to the single process live in a deployment-wide section of the same document. A browser holds a single tenant session at a time — reaching a different tenant requires logging out first — and startup payment polling resumes for every configured tenant. A single-tenant deployment is a one-entry document, which a script writes from the environment variables used before.
